title: LossChart and LossTab duplicate loss-curve logic that has already diverged (stale 'same logic' claim)
description: LossChart.tsx and LossTab.tsx independently re-implement the same loss-curve pipeline: filter iteration keys, find train_/eval_ keys, gather y-values, compute yMin/yMax/yRange, xScale/yScale, makePath, and the best-iteration clamp. The LossChart doc-comment is not the source of this note, but LossTab.tsx:4 explicitly says 'Same logic as LossChart.tsx'. They have already drifted apart on finite-value handling and best-iteration clamping (see the bug findings above), which is exactly the failure mode of copy-paste duplication. Extracting the shared scaling/path helpers (e.g. a `useLossCurveGeometry(lossHistory, bestIteration)` hook returning { trainKey, evalKey, makePath, bestX, isEmpty }) into one module would remove the divergence and let both the sidebar and full-size charts share one hardened implementation.
evidence: LossChart.tsx:18-49 mirrors LossTab.tsx:38-100 (key discovery, allVals reduce for yMin/yMax, xScale/yScale closures, makePath, bestX). LossTab.tsx:4 'Same logic as LossChart.tsx'.
est_reduction: ~30-40 lines of duplicated scaling/path logic consolidated into one shared helper
behavior_preservation: Behavior-changing if unified on the hardened LossTab version (fixes the NaN/clamp bugs); if pure consolidation is desired, the shared helper must reproduce each chart's current sizing/margins and empty-state, leaving rendered output identical for finite data.
